decisions.reason: SOL keeps the sense that the movement goes beyond attack and defense.
“Either” naturally connects to the two concepts just named.
SOL preserves the question surfacing and the spear-raising action.
The source says the Breath blankets the sky; “across” drops that covering image.
An umbrella without ribs is different from one without its canopy.
SOL preserves the unpredictable result of the tiny movement.
The widened pupils are preserved without changing the action.
The subject remains clear from context, and time’s rapid flow resumes.
The source describes the pillar as splitting in progress; SOL changes it to a completed action.
“Continued to split” makes the source’s “even now” continuation clear.
The source’s emphatic “how on earth” question is reduced to “How?”
Naming Morgoth here is a clear, faithful subject reference.
The shorter repeated phrasing preserves his disguises and accumulated experience.
SOL drops Morgoth’s name despite the source explicitly repeating it.
“How was such a thing possible?” preserves the question’s sense.
“Within” naturally preserves the energy-flow image.
“No more than empty echoes” keeps the same meaning.
The source says he couldn’t properly answer, not that he couldn’t have answered.
The deep, distant retreat of his consciousness is preserved.
“Followed what he saw” conveys acting only on what was visible.
The redirected magical power still forms the rounded barrier around him.
“From the outside” preserves the contrast with how it appears to others.
The darkness and the lights seen through his blue-black eyes remain intact.
The omitted name is clear from context and does not alter the viewpoint.
The dazzling white and unfathomably deep darkness are both preserved.
The glossary’s established rendering is “Magic”; SOL substitutes “spells.”
SOL preserves the thousands of potential deaths and his gratitude that he is the target.
The counterfactual danger to his allies is preserved.
Both the summoned spear and the instinctive dantian action remain.
“Opened his Middle Dantian” preserves the source’s action and comparison.
The spear’s speed, flame, and piercing of each spell’s core are preserved.
The sky and earth shaking is unchanged.
SOL replaces the sky’s dazzling display with added bursts of color.
The source says the Dragonheart’s magical power lies dormant; SOL drops that detail.
The pressure is conveyed through the spearhead, not described as bearing down.
The knee rising from deep in the ground under the Breath is preserved.
“There was no other choice” preserves the necessity of going.
“For now” fits the source’s “at this moment” better than “just this once.”
“Slipping out of place” conveys the bones’ misalignment without changing the injury.
The magical power threatens to swallow both his body and spearhead.
The unsteady first-step image is preserved.
The footprint still conveys the unusual weight of his strength and Will.
The preceding sentence supplies the subject; the source says Magic cannot hold him back.
The vines tear and the immense gravity weakens, with the comparison retained.
“Another” works as a concise continuation of the established step rhythm.
“Advanced” preserves his slow, unhesitating movement.
The shadow, dreamlike vision, and spearhead serving as a torch remain.
The source says the comrade would willingly brave any danger; SOL weakens and narrows that commitment.
The Grand Mage’s roar-like cry still rings through the din.
The reddened sky, fireballs, and their target are all preserved.
The source says the heat rushes in; SOL makes the completed spell itself rush toward him.
SOL omits that Morgoth is unstartled by this sudden attack.
The angry sneer at a magical rather than bladed attack is preserved.
The source emphatically says he is no one but a Dragon; SOL removes that emphasis.
The Dragon species’ mastery of Magic and Morgoth’s former leadership are preserved.
Not needing to speak preserves the source’s point that he needn’t say it aloud.
His will, greater magical power, and unreachable realm are preserved.
The generic human mana is preserved; singular phrasing works here.
The ash scatters and Johnson coughs blood and falls while fighting the Guardians.
“Deadliest” preserves the source’s description of the injury as most fatal.
The blood-soaked lips and gentle smile are preserved.
The source describes a brief opening, not a distraction, that let someone be free of gravity.
The faint words and barely moving lips are both retained.
The source locates the flame at the tip of his foot as it touches down; SOL shifts it around the foot.
The established term is “Magic,” and SOL also recasts its range as a spell’s range.
The compressed energy and explosion are preserved.
The Dragon Breath’s line-like stretch and Taekyung’s charge through it remain.
The Breath’s increasing fierceness and Morgoth’s growing sense of danger are preserved.
The source’s corrective emphasis “if anything, rather” is dropped in SOL.
SOL drops the image of roars and screams blanketing the battlefield.
“Pressed on” preserves his forward movement without hesitation.
The shadow looming like a mountain and his instinctive realization remain.
The unprecedented sight is conveyed directly and faithfully.
The spearhead rises through and cleaves the pillar of darkness.
“In an instant” preserves the source’s brief timespan.
The Breath’s spent power and dispersal of the darkness are retained.
The human’s role in dispersing the Breath is stated clearly.
Morgoth wonders where it went wrong while watching the sight.
The snowball image and its crash back upon him are preserved.
“Barely a hundred years to live” preserves the mortal’s lifespan.
The separate fragments retain both of Morgoth’s titles.
The slowed world, muttering, and wing-spreading action are unchanged.
SOL drops the figure’s image of shooting skyward and cutting through the heavens.
The two weapons tearing through space toward each other is clear from context.
The source specifies a slash of the claw; “brought down” loses that physical action.
The realization at the same instant is preserved.
The source says the foreleg he had just swung was already cut; SOL places him mid-swing.
The wound’s persistence after his return to true form is preserved.
SOL explicitly assigns the trophy view to Morgoth, where the source leaves the subject unstated.
The source hedges that the game might be ending; SOL makes it certain.
“Premonitions” changes the source’s instinctive intuition into foreknowledge.
The low, sharp slicing sound is preserved.
The spearhead’s Will-driven cut into the friend’s final trace is preserved.
